supporting_observations.claim: The alerted change occurred at 13:42:41.963 UTC: dev.sharma added hana.ito to Billing-Share, not Remote Desktop Users.
The group-change SubjectLogonId 0x1307103b matches a dev.sharma Kerberos network logon on DC-RB-01 from 10.60.10.23. Endpoint telemetry identifies that address as WS-DSHARMA-01.

The target group, administrator account, originating workstation, and afternoon timing match the supplied change calendar and group-management practices. This supports a benign disposition for the alerted addition.

The subsequent RDP logon to DC-RB-01 was also dev.sharma from WS-DSHARMA-01, but used a different logon ID, 0x13076620, and occurred after the group addition. It should not be treated as the session that performed the change.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection-status metadata reports missing PROXY-RB-01 proxy logs from 13:30 through 14:15 UTC. This limits visibility into web activity but does not prevent attribution of the directory change through S28-00016 and S28-00018.
claims_not_established: The actual approval ticket was not supplied; S28-00018 records the change, not its approval. Authorization is supported by consistency with the supplied change calendar rather than direct ticket evidence.
S28-00016 and S28-00018 identify the account and session used, but do not independently prove the human operator's identity.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: hana.ito's UserAssist entries on WS-HITO-01 reference powershell.exe at 13:49:41 and mstsc.exe at 14:11:25 after decoding the ROT13 value names. These registry updates do not establish command arguments, an RDP destination, or successful remote administration, and do not establish misuse of the Billing-Share addition (S28-00043, S28-00054).

Separate software-policy review: dev.sharma launched Firefox with https://zoom.us/ and executed ZSATray.exe; a Zscaler DLL had a valid signature. These products are not listed in the supplied approved-software inventory, but these records do not establish malicious activity or a connection to the group change (S28-00009, S28-00030, S28-00032).

Separate session-timeline review: WS-DSHARMA-01 logged a lock at 13:47:41, then an mstsc.exe launch and successful FILE-RB-01 RDP logon before the recorded unlock at 13:59:53. The records do not establish the explanation or link this sequence to abuse of the earlier group addition (S28-00033, S28-00034, S28-00038, S28-00050).
